usage.final_text:
I found and fixed all five problems from INC-5521. The full suite passes (26 tests, 0 failures), and 16 of the 18 new tests fail on the original code, so they do reproduce the bugs.

## Causes

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| 263 orders for 250 units | Every mutator reads a SKU record, changes it and writes it back, with no lock. Two concurrent reserves both see the same free stock, and one write overwrites the other. `addStock` racing a `reserve` could also wipe out held units. |
| `reserved` went negative and stayed there | `release()` never refused a committed order. `expire()` released every order older than the TTL whatever its status, including committed ones, and checked the status before any concurrent `commit` finished. |
| A retry held stock twice | The "does this order already exist?" check wasn't atomic, so an overlapping retry passed it too and held the stock again. The nightly `expire` then "released" the committed order, which happened to cancel the extra hold. That's why it seemed to go away when the reservation expired. |
| A bundle item stayed held after the order was rejected | `reserve` held each item as it went and threw at the out-of-stock item without undoing the earlier ones. No order record was written, so nothing could ever release them. |
| `sold` higher than orders shipped | A retried `commit`, or `commit` racing `release`/`expire`, could apply twice. |

## Fix
- **`src/keyed-lock.js` (new):** a lock per key. Calls on the same key take turns in arrival order; calls on different keys never wait for each other.
- **`src/inventory.js`:**
  - Each operation locks its order first, then its SKUs in sorted order. That fixed order prevents deadlocks, including between bundles that list the same items in different orders.
  - `reserve` checks every item before holding any.
  - `release` rejects committed orders with `OrderStateError`.
  - `expire` re-reads each order under its lock and only releases orders that are still `reserved`.
  - The methods, arguments, return values and error types are unchanged, and `src/store.js` is untouched.
- **No service-wide lock:** calls that share no SKU and no order still don't wait for each other. Two tests check this by stalling one call's store access while calls on other SKUs and orders complete.
- **Shared stores:** locks belong to the store object, so two services built on the same store also coordinate.

## Tests
`tests/concurrency.test.js` has 18 tests:
- **Reproductions:** at least one per symptom, e.g. 300 buyers for 250 units, restocking during a sale, commit vs release, expire vs commit, overlapping expire runs, overlapping retries, all-or-nothing bundles and double commits.
- **No-waiting checks:** the two stalled-store tests. They pass on the original code too, since it has no locks at all.
- **Mixed load:** a random concurrent workload that checks all counters against the order records.

I also ran the suite 15 times with no failures, plus 600 extra randomized runs (not kept in the repo) against a store that doesn't copy values and one with no latency. No locks were left held.

## Limits
- **One process only:** the locks work within one Node process. Your store offers only `get`, `set` and `keys`, with no atomic operation, so separate worker processes sharing one Redis can't coordinate through it. If the 40 workers are separate processes, that needs a store-level primitive such as Redis `WATCH`/`MULTI` or a Lua script, which this task's constraints ruled out.
- **Store write failures:** if the store fails partway through updating a bundle, some items can still end up held. That's a failure-recovery gap, not part of this incident.

Nothing is committed yet.
